Lemma
[degree-2 homogeneity: strict positivity for every nonzero velocity]

↗ lem:dc-ch3-4-1-posnbhd ↗ lem:dc-ch3-2-6

1. ch3:4.1The value $G(q,v)=\frac{\partial ^2 F}{\partial t^2}(0,q,v)$ is degree-2 homogeneous in the chart velocity: $G(q,cv)=c^2\, G(q,v)$. Consequently the neighborhood $V$ of section 3 satisfies $G(q,v)>0$ for every $q\in V$ and every nonzero chart velocity $v$, removing the unit-speed restriction.
Proof

\sketch

Under $v\mapsto cv$ every building block of $G$ scales: $D(\exp _p^{-1})_a(cv)=c\, D(\exp _p^{-1})_a(v)$, $D^2(\exp _p^{-1})_a(cv,cv)=c^2\, D^2(\exp _p^{-1})_a(v,v)$, and the geodesic acceleration $-\Gamma _a(cv,cv)=c^2\, \big(-\Gamma _a(v,v)\big)$ by the degree-2 homogeneity of the Christoffel contraction (the coordinate form of the homogeneity subsection 1.1); since $\langle \cdot ,\cdot \rangle _p$ is bilinear both summands acquire the factor $c^2$. Writing a nonzero $v=|v|\, (v/|v|)$ with $v/|v|$ of unit chart norm, $G(q,v)=|v|^2\, G(q,v/|v|)>0$ by section 3.

□
